correctness.rationale: The proof reduces cop-win to induced trees on triangle-free graphs, classifies every permissible column word by three forbidden adjacent pairs, derives exact two-state transitions, counts interval placements and independently derives each binomial coefficient via singleton gaps. Rational probability substitution and first-moment differentiation are symbolic identities. The provided verifier exhaustively compares 349515 induced graphs for \(1\le n\le9\), directly tests dismantling for \(n\le7\), and checks 100 full coefficient rows; finite tests support but do not replace the infinite proof.

evidence: Vince treats all connected subsets; induced cyclic connected subsets are present and the reported limiting density is \(3/4\), versus \(2/3\) here.
Ahmed--Cameron define the size-refined cop-win polynomial, but their stated target classes have cycle rank one or two. \(L_n\) has cycle rank \(n-1\), outside that scope for \(n\ge4\).
Their full articles were not inspected in their entirety, so complete exclusions are not asserted.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A connected-subset mean or an unweighted connected-set count does not determine how many sets are acyclic at every size. A classification confined to one- and two-cycle graphs cannot directly cover the all-n ladder polynomial; exact small ladders may be previously covered.

value.rationale: The induced-vertex-set distribution by size is the complete input to the node cop-win reliability curve at arbitrary \(p\), not determined by existing grid tables of total and largest induced trees. Its explicit all-n rational generating function, exact coefficient sum and conditional mean refine a natural network-failure model and distinguish its asymptotic \(2/3\) successful-set density from the \(3/4\) connected-set result. No wider-grid theorem is claimed.
